focus: Define accuracy, cost, and trustworthy-evaluation improvements for the measured fetched-text screen.
noveltyJustification: Six findings add new evaluation and cost controls; three partly extend the earlier comparator, stability, and operational-scope findings.
keyQuestions: What drove the measured Jev result?
How can accuracy improve or cost fall?
How can the measurement become more trustworthy?
Where else in .skilled would the same judgment pay off?
What would default-on integration need, cost, and risk?
answeredQuestions: How can accuracy improve or cost fall?
How can the measurement become more trustworthy?
ruledOut: Use a lexical miss as a clean verdict or as permission to skip Jev: the measured pattern screen caught only 1 of 30 planted sentences.
Treat three reruns of each fixed row as independent examples or as evidence of source/domain generalization.
Treat text detection as sanitization or as authorization for a tool action; detection and mitigation are separate decisions.
focusTrackReason: The prior iteration's recommended next focus was accuracy/cost plus a measurement design that separates repeated-call stability from independent generalization.
partialSuccess: No additional Jev run was made; the analysis uses the recorded live result and independent published evaluation guidance. A no-run means cost changes are design estimates, not measured deltas.

title: Separate malicious injection from benign agent-directed instructions
claim: The current binary target labels rows only as instructs or clean, while its prompt asks about behavior-changing agent instructions. Keep those dimensions distinct: label malicious authority-changing attempts, legitimate agent instructions, quoted attacks, and ordinary prose separately, then map them to an operational policy.

title: Do not use lexical misses to avoid semantic screening
claim: The four-pattern screen caught one planted attack in the measured result. A cheap lexical hit can trigger added scrutiny, but a miss is not a supported clean verdict and does not safely reduce classifier calls.

title: Separate threshold bands from action authorization
claim: The scorer already reports separate review/flag/block rates at 0.25, 0.50, and 0.75. Treat these as score bands: annotate or route uncertain text for review, and use independent deterministic permissions/action screening for consequential tool calls.

title: Production request cost should use one measured screening pass per exposed payload
claim: The benchmark makes three fresh calls per row plus one auth test, so this 90-row run planned 271 calls and has a measured p50/p95 call latency of 324/388 ms. A serving path should budget one classifier pass per fetched payload (or per bounded chunk for long payloads); keep reruns for benchmark stability rather than paying them on every production fetch.

title: Measure cost as calls, input tokens, and end-to-end latency
claim: The scorer estimates input tokens as payload characters divided by four and multiplies by three reruns; it records call latency but not end-to-end interception overhead or monetary spend. Report per-fetch call count, normalized input tokens, p50/p95 added latency, retries, timeout rate, and cache-hit rate before estimating a production cost.

title: Audit labels independently and preserve disagreement
claim: All 60 natural labels are operator-delegated and all 30 planted labels are construction labels; the benchmark has only five natural positive examples. Add a second blind labeler and adjudication on ambiguous rows, then retain agreement and label provenance so benign instructions are not silently conflated with attacks.

title: Freeze a multi-axis holdout instead of relying on aggregate accuracy
claim: Use source/domain-held-out real fetches and separate hard-benign, obfuscated, multilingual, HTML/Markdown, search-snippet, and structural-shift slices at fixed thresholds. Report recall, benign false-positive rate, precision, and calibration by slice, not one aggregate score. PIDS-Bench reports a detector with held-out F1 above 0.98 but roughly one-third false positives on one external benign slice; that result is a caution about aggregate metrics, not a prediction for Jev.

title: Report sample uncertainty separately from call stability
claim: The 90 row outcomes produce naive row-independent 95% Wilson intervals of about 82–95% for accuracy, 71–94% for precision, and 74–95% for recall. The three calls per row estimate within-row decision stability, not independent corpus uncertainty; source-cluster bootstrap intervals and a held-out source set are needed because rows share source groups.

title: Detection and mitigation require separate validation
claim: An injection score can flag content but does not demonstrate accurate removal. Evaluate any quarantine or sanitization step separately for attack text removed and useful content retained.
